title: Hands Fold a Paper Sheet
tests: Tests coherent hand anatomy, hand-object contact and a completed paper-folding action in one text-generated shot.

faults.what: The clip contains audible speech, transcribed as "Sos!", despite the explicit no-sound requirement.
The action takes place on a plain white surface rather than the requested visibly wooden table.

judge.summary: The clip convincingly shows blue paper being folded and creased, but uses a white surface instead of a wooden table and includes unwanted sound.

must_haves.item: Both human hands and the entire blue sheet remain visible on a wooden table.
must_haves.why: Both hands and the sheet stay in view in the supplied frames, but the surface is plain white with no visible wood texture.

must_haves.item: The hands visibly bring one half of the sheet over the other, producing a folded sheet rather than an abrupt object replacement.
must_haves.why: The frames show the flat sheet, a lifted half being folded over, and the resulting folded rectangle.

must_haves.item: The hands press along the resulting crease after folding.
must_haves.why: The later frames show fingers pressing and smoothing the folded paper along its crease.

must_haves.item: Hands remain anatomically plausible, without extra or fused fingers, and make convincing contact with the paper.
must_haves.why: The visible hands have plausible anatomy and grip, hold, and press the paper convincingly.

must_haves.item: The blue paper remains a single consistent object throughout the action.
must_haves.why: The sheet remains plain blue and shows a coherent progression from flat paper to a folded rectangle, without visible replacement or duplication.

must_haves.item: The eight-second widescreen video uses one fixed overhead shot and has no sound.
must_haves.why: The supplied duration is eight seconds and the frames show a consistent widescreen overhead view, but the audio report explicitly identifies speech.
